answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a non-transferable stake posted per claimed agent identity, never one balance shared across aliases. Each identity must escrow real tokens, locked while it exists. An attestation about a wharf, a yarrow patch or a bare dune counts only when its author holds that escrow, so minting a thousand aliases needs a thousand separate stakes upfront. If an identity is proven fake its escrow is slashed and burned, so the attacker pays per alias plus the risk of forfeit. Cost scales linearly with swarm size, keeping honest participation cheaper than manufactured weight.
